For any set $S,$ we have $|P(S)|={2}^{|S|}.$ Also, $|S\times T|=|S|\cdot |T|.$

In our case, 

$$
|A|=1,\,|B|=2.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(A)| & ={2}^{|A|}={2}^{1}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(P(A))| & ={2}^{|P(A)|} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(P(A))\times B| & =|P(P(A))|\cdot |B| \\  & =4\cdot 2 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
